svg.title: The same server over stdio and over Streamable HTTP
svg.desc: Two columns of identical width and identical row heights compare the same server run two ways. On the left, headed stdio, the host spawns your process: Claude Desktop, Cursor and Zed each point down at their own accent-coloured box, process one, process two and process three, each holding its own index. A panel below gives the command, uv with an absolute directory running the knowledge_base module, and notes that there is one process per host with its own copy of the corpus, that it is configured by absolute path with no network and no port, that standard output is the protocol channel so one stray print ends the connection, that the host owns the process lifetime and collects standard error, and that this is the right default for a desktop host and for a first run. On the right, headed Streamable HTTP, the server is already running: Claude Code, VS Code and Gemini CLI all converge on one wide accent box reading one process, one index, posting to the mcp path on loopback port 8000. Its panel gives the command with the http flag and notes one process for every host and one place to update the corpus, configuration by URL with Gemini CLI wanting it under httpUrl, a measured pair of responses where the mcp path answers 200 and the same path with a trailing slash answers 307, marked as a redirect and not a 404, and a warning that off loopback you must pass transport security or every call is a 421. A band across the bottom holds the identical source files, unchanged between the two columns, and states that the tools, schemas, annotations and instructions are the same and that the transport is chosen by one command-line flag.
svg.text: Same code. The only question is who owns the process.
Three hosts and three indexes on the left. Three hosts and one on the right.
One process per host, each with its own copy of the corpus.
Configured by an absolute path. No network and no port.
stdout is the protocol channel; one stray print() ends it.
The host owns the process lifetime and collects stderr.
The right default for a desktop host, and for a first run.
One process for every host. One place to update the corpus.
Configured by a URL. Gemini CLI wants it under "httpUrl".
Off loopback, pass transport_security or every call is a 421.
src/knowledge_base/ index.py tools.py resources.py prompts.py app.py
Same tools, same schemas, same annotations, same instructions. The transport is one command-line flag.
